verses.text: It shall be, when you have come in to the land which Yahweh your God gives you for an inheritance, possess it, and dwell in it,

that you shall take some of the first of all the fruit of the ground, which you shall bring in from your land that Yahweh your God gives you. You shall put it in a basket, and shall go to the place which Yahweh your God shall choose, to cause his name to dwell there.
You shall come to the priest who shall be in those days, and tell him, “I profess today to Yahweh your God, that I have come to the land which Yahweh swore to our fathers to give us.”
The priest shall take the basket out of your hand, and set it down before Yahweh your God’s altar.

You shall answer and say before Yahweh your God, “My father  was a Syrian ready to perish. He went down into Egypt, and lived there, few in number. There he became a great, mighty, and populous nation.
The Egyptians mistreated us, afflicted us, and imposed hard labor on us.
Then we cried to Yahweh, the God of our fathers. Yahweh heard our voice, and saw our affliction, our toil, and our oppression.
Yahweh brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand, with an outstretched arm, with great terror, with signs, and with wonders;
and he has brought us into this place, and has given us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
Now, behold, I have brought the first of the fruit of the ground, which you, Yahweh, have given me.” You shall set it down before Yahweh your God, and worship before Yahweh your God.
You shall rejoice in all the good which Yahweh your God has given to you, and to your house, you, and the Levite, and the foreigner who is among you.

When you have finished tithing all the tithe of your increase in the third year, which is the year of tithing, then you shall give it to the Levite, to the foreigner, to the fatherless, and to the widow, that they may eat within your gates, and be filled.

You shall say before Yahweh your God, “I have put away the holy things out of my house, and also have given them to the Levite, to the foreigner, to the fatherless, and to the widow, according to all your commandment which you have commanded me. I have not transgressed any of your commandments, neither have I forgotten them.

I have not eaten of it in my mourning, neither have I removed any of it while I was unclean, nor given of it for the dead. I have listened to Yahweh my God’s voice. I have done according to all that you have commanded me.
Look down from your holy habitation, from heaven, and bless your people Israel, and the ground which you have given us, as you swore to our fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.”
Today Yahweh your God commands you to do these statutes and ordinances. You shall therefore keep and do them with all your heart and with all your soul.
You have declared today that Yahweh is your God, and that you would walk in his ways, and keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his ordinances, and listen to his voice.
Yahweh has declared today that you are a people for his own possession, as he has promised you, and that you should keep all his commandments.
He will make you high above all nations that he has made, in praise, in name, and in honor; and that you may be a holy people to Yahweh your God, as he has spoken.

footnotes.content: Notice how the Lord begins with a promise—you will *have* come in. He speaks as though your arrival is certain before you even take the first step. He sees the end from the beginning, and wants you to know you are already home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The firstfruits go in a basket—a simple vessel—and are carried to the Lord's chosen place. There is dignity even in our smallest offering when it is given to Him first, not as an afterthought. He sees the fruit, not the basket.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I profess today"—there is something about standing before God and speaking aloud what He has done. Witness is not just private gratitude; it is spoken, public, real. When we tell the priest, we are telling the whole community what we have learned of His faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priest receives your basket and sets it before the altar—your hands open, your gift released. There is a moment of relinquishment in every true offering. We cannot hold what we have given to the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "My father was a Syrian ready to perish." Before there was a nation, there was a wandering man—Jacob—with nothing but a promise. You are invited to remember not the glory, but the smallness, the desperation, the bare thread by which you hold your existence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Egyptians mistreated, afflicted, imposed hard labor. The text names the suffering plainly, without dressing it up. Sometimes faith is not about forgetting pain, but about telling it truly and knowing the Lord was there even so.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "We cried to Yahweh." A cry is not a polished prayer—it is raw, desperate, the sound of those who have nowhere else to go. And listen: He *heard* our voice, *saw* our affliction. The Lord does not merely know; He listens. He looks.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A mighty hand, an outstretched arm, signs and wonders—the language of divine might appearing for the weak. Jesus later speaks of laying down His life; here we see the pattern: power used not to dominate, but to deliver those who cry out.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From Egypt to the promised land: a land flowing with milk and honey. Abundance follows deliverance. The Lord does not free us and leave us in the wilderness—He brings us to plenty. He completes what He begins.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I have brought the first of the fruit *which you have given me." Even our gift to Him is already His. We are merely offering back what was never ours to begin with. Gratitude is the truest surrender—acknowledging that all good flows from His hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rejoice together: you, the Levite, the foreigner. Notice how joy is meant to be shared, especially with those who have less. Blessing is not meant to divide the table; it is meant to widen it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The third-year tithe goes to Levite, foreigner, fatherless, widow—those with no land, no lineage, no standing. A whole year's tithe dedicated to the invisible ones. The law of Moses was written in their favor.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I have not transgressed any of your commandments, neither have I forgotten them." A conscience at rest—not perfect, but faithful. The speaker is reciting obedience, holding it up as a fragile but real thing. Obedience, kept.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Not eaten in mourning, not given for the dead—consecrated food kept sacred. Even grief does not give us leave to profane what we have set apart for Him. Holiness holds even in our sorrow.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Look down from your holy habitation, from heaven." A prayer that the Lord will bend His gaze toward His people, toward their fields, toward what they labor for. The Lord's attention is itself a blessing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Today Yahweh your God commands you." And "You shall therefore keep and do them with all your heart and all your soul." Not by force, but by love—keeping the law becomes an act of heart-devotion when you see the Lord who gave it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A declaration of covenant—you have said aloud that Yahweh is your God. Words spoken before witnesses bind the heart. In Jesus, we too make this declaration: I will follow Him, walk in His ways, obey, listen. Word made flesh, lived out.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "A people for his own possession." You belong to the Lord as surely as a child belongs to their parent. There is security in that belonging—you are claimed, known, treasured. That is your identity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo of this promise: the Lord still lifts up those who make Him their God. Not yet in earthly praise and honor as Israel knew it, but in something deeper—the honor of being known by the Savior, set apart as His own, called holy. That is a height no earthly nation can match.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
